card.name: Table cells just before next entry
card.fires_on: The last token of a table cell or dosing row in flattened label tables, such as a unit, number digit or word ending, right before the next row or column starts.

modes.label: Number or unit ending a cell
modes.description: A final digit or unit like kg ends a dosing or dosimetry table cell before the next entry.
modes.example: Greater than or equal to 40<< kg>> Darunavir 800

modes.label: Word ending a table cell
modes.description: A closing word piece of a drug name or phrase ends a cell or heading before new text.
modes.example: on epoetin al<<fa>> Adult patients with CKD not on dial

modes.label: Dosing schedule phrase end
modes.description: A final word of a schedule or instruction phrase sits just before the next table column.
modes.example: Week 49 and every 4 weeks<< thereafter>> Subsequent treatment doses 76 mg

card.writes: Promoted and suppressed tokens look like code or formatting junk, so no clear output effect.
card.plain: It marks the end of an entry in a flattened dosing table, just before the next entry begins.
